description: Stable RtoGtoR error codes. Codes are never reused or renumbered. Deprecated codes stay in this file with "deprecated": true.

codes.title: Unsupported specification version
codes.meaning: The document declares a specVersion whose major version this engine does not support.
codes.remediation: Upgrade the engine, or write the document against a supported specVersion (see `rtogtor version`).

codes.title: Mapping does not match the schema
codes.meaning: The mapping document is well-formed JSON/YAML but violates specs/mapping.schema.json.
codes.remediation: Fix the field reported at the given path. Validate with `rtogtor validate --mapping <file>`.

codes.title: Mapping cannot be read or parsed
codes.meaning: The mapping file could not be read, or it is not valid JSON or YAML (including duplicate keys).
codes.remediation: Check the file path and syntax. Files ending in .json are parsed as JSON; .yaml and .yml as YAML.

codes.title: Duplicate entity name
codes.meaning: Two entities in the mapping share the same name. Entity names define identities and must be unique.
codes.remediation: Rename one of the entities.

codes.title: Unknown entity reference
codes.meaning: A relationship refers to an entity name that is not defined in the mapping.
codes.remediation: Define the entity, or correct the name in the relationship.

codes.title: Key field not mapped
codes.meaning: A field listed in an entity's key is not mapped as one of that entity's properties.
codes.remediation: Add a property mapping for the key field, or remove it from the key.

codes.title: Key field type not allowed in identity
codes.meaning: A key field has a logical type that cannot be an identity component (for example float64 or json). See specs/identity.md §2.
codes.remediation: Choose a different key, or convert the field to a permitted type.

codes.title: Foreign key does not match the referenced key
codes.meaning: The number of foreign-key columns differs from the number of key fields of the referenced entity.
codes.remediation: List one foreign-key column per key field of the referenced entity, in the same order.

codes.title: Duplicate property name
codes.meaning: Two property mappings of the same entity or relationship produce the same destination property name.
codes.remediation: Rename one of the properties.

codes.title: Duplicate column mapping
codes.meaning: The same source column is mapped more than once within one entity or relationship.
codes.remediation: Remove the duplicate mapping.

codes.title: Direction not yet implemented
codes.meaning: The mapping is valid, but this engine version cannot yet execute mappings in the declared direction.
codes.remediation: Check `docs/roadmap.md` for when the direction is planned.

codes.title: Duplicate relationship name
codes.meaning: Two relationships in the mapping share the same name.
codes.remediation: Rename one of the relationships.

codes.title: Reserved property name
codes.meaning: A property mapping uses the name of the identity property (default rtg_id), which the engine manages.
codes.remediation: Rename the property, or change identity.property.

codes.title: Invalid value for logical type
codes.meaning: A value is not a valid encoding of its logical type as defined in specs/values.md.
codes.remediation: Correct the value. The message names the type and the reason.

codes.title: Unknown or unsupported logical type
codes.meaning: The logical type name is not defined in specs/values.md, or the operation does not support that type.
codes.remediation: Use one of the logical types listed in specs/values.md §1.

codes.title: Null identity component
codes.meaning: A key field is null, so no identity can be derived for the record.
codes.remediation: Ensure key fields are NOT NULL in the source, or choose a different key.

codes.title: Type not permitted in identity
codes.meaning: A key component has a logical type that is not permitted in rtg-id/v1 (specs/identity.md §2).
codes.remediation: Use a key made of permitted types.

codes.title: Empty identity input
codes.meaning: The entity type is empty or invalid UTF-8, or the key has no components.
codes.remediation: Declare a non-empty entity name and at least one key field.

codes.title: Unsupported column type
codes.meaning: A column's database type has no logical type in this specification version. Inspection reports it with a null logical type; mappings cannot use the column.
codes.remediation: Leave the column unmapped, or convert it in the source (for example with a view) to a supported type. See specs/values.md §7.

codes.title: Table has no primary key
codes.meaning: The table has no primary key, so it has no stable identity and cannot be read resumably. Strict mappings cannot use it as an entity.
codes.remediation: Add a primary key, or declare a unique NOT NULL key in the mapping when that is supported.

codes.title: Schema not found
codes.meaning: A requested database schema (namespace) does not exist or is not visible to the connecting user.
codes.remediation: Check the schema name (names are case-sensitive) and the user's privileges.

codes.title: Cannot connect to the database
codes.meaning: The engine could not open a connection: the server is unreachable, refused the connection, or rejected the credentials.
codes.remediation: Check that the server is running and reachable and that the credentials are correct. Connection details are never printed.

codes.title: Connection settings missing or invalid
codes.meaning: The environment variable that should hold the connection URL is not set, is empty, or does not contain a valid URL.
codes.remediation: Set the variable named by --source-env (for example SOURCE_URL) to a URL such as postgres://user:password@host:5432/dbname.

codes.title: PostgreSQL query failed
codes.meaning: A query issued by the PostgreSQL adapter failed. The message includes the SQLSTATE when the server provided one.
codes.remediation: Check the connecting user's privileges on the catalog and the inspected schemas. If the failure persists, report it with the SQLSTATE.

codes.title: Mapped table not found
codes.meaning: A table named by an entity or relationship does not exist in the inspected source schema.
codes.remediation: Check the table and schema names in the mapping (names are case-sensitive).

codes.title: Mapped column not found
codes.meaning: A column named by the mapping (property, key or foreign-key column) does not exist in its source table.
codes.remediation: Check the column name, or re-run `rtogtor inspect` to see the table's columns.

codes.title: Declared type does not match the source
codes.meaning: A property's declared logical type differs from the column's inspected logical type, or the column's type is unsupported.
codes.remediation: Change the property's type to the inspected type shown in the message.

codes.title: Key column is nullable
codes.meaning: A key column allows NULL in the source. Rows with a NULL key cannot get an identity and will be recorded as failed records.
codes.remediation: Add a NOT NULL constraint in the source, or accept that such rows fail with RTG-ID-001.

codes.title: Lossy transformation not allowed
codes.meaning: Under the strict loss policy, a property would be stored in a lossy way (specs/values.md §5) and no policies.allow entry covers it.
codes.remediation: Add a policies.allow entry with a reason for this loss, use the flexible policy, or leave the property unmapped.

codes.title: Feature not yet supported by this engine
codes.meaning: The mapping is valid but uses a feature this engine version cannot execute yet (for example junction relationships, natural identity, or some types).
codes.remediation: Check docs/roadmap.md and docs/limitations.md; restructure the mapping to avoid the feature for now.

codes.title: Foreign key does not match the referenced key types
codes.meaning: A foreign-key column's logical type differs from the corresponding key field of the referenced entity, so identities could never match.
codes.remediation: Map foreign keys only onto keys of the same logical type, in the same order.

codes.title: Record could not be converted
codes.meaning: A source value could not be converted for the destination (for example an array containing NULL, which Neo4j cannot store). The record was written to the failed-records store.
codes.remediation: Inspect the record with `rtogtor failures --run-id <id>`, fix the source data, and resume or re-run.

codes.title: Relationship endpoint not found
codes.meaning: A relationship could not be created because one of its end nodes does not exist in the destination, usually because that node's own record failed.
codes.remediation: Fix the failed end-node record, then re-run; relationship writes are idempotent.

codes.title: Batch write failed
codes.meaning: Writing a batch to the destination failed after the configured retries. The batch was not committed and no checkpoint was recorded.
codes.remediation: Check the destination's health, then resume the run with --resume; committed batches are not repeated.

codes.title: Run interrupted
codes.meaning: The run stopped before completing (cancellation or an injected fault). Every committed batch is checkpointed.
codes.remediation: Resume the run with `rtogtor migrate --resume <run-id>`.

codes.title: Run not found
codes.meaning: No run with the given ID exists in the state directory.
codes.remediation: Check the run ID and --state-dir. Runs are listed in the state directory's runs/ folder.

codes.title: Mapping changed since the run started
codes.meaning: Resuming requires the identical mapping, but its canonical hash differs from the one recorded when the run started.
codes.remediation: Resume with the original mapping, or start a new run.

codes.title: Run already completed
codes.meaning: The run finished; there is nothing to resume.
codes.remediation: Start a new run. Re-running a migration is safe because writes are idempotent.

codes.title: Run state unreadable
codes.meaning: The run-state files are missing, corrupt, or written by an incompatible specification version.
codes.remediation: Do not edit run-state files by hand. Start a new run; idempotent writes make this safe.

codes.title: Neo4j query failed
codes.meaning: A query issued by the Neo4j adapter failed. The message includes the Neo4j status code.
codes.remediation: Check the user's privileges and the database name. Retryable cluster errors are retried automatically.

codes.title: Entity missing in destination
codes.meaning: A source record's identity has no node in the destination.
codes.remediation: Check `rtogtor failures` for the record; re-run or resume the migration.

codes.title: Entity count mismatch
codes.meaning: The destination holds a different number of nodes for an entity than the source has rows (for example extra nodes from other sources sharing the label).
codes.remediation: Investigate extra nodes with the entity's label, or give the entity a dedicated label.

codes.title: Relationship count mismatch
codes.meaning: The number of relationships of a mapped type differs from the number expected from the source.
codes.remediation: Check `rtogtor failures` for relationship records, then re-run; relationship writes are idempotent.

codes.title: Dangling source reference
codes.meaning: Source rows reference keys that do not exist in the referenced table (the mapping's foreign key is not enforced by the source). No relationship can be created for them.
codes.remediation: Fix the source data or add a foreign-key constraint.

codes.title: Unsupported protocol version
codes.meaning: A protocol message declares a protocolVersion whose major version the engine does not support.
codes.remediation: Use an SDK version compatible with this engine (see specs/compatibility.md).

codes.title: Invalid command-line usage
codes.meaning: A command was given unknown flags, missing required flags, or invalid flag values.
codes.remediation: Run the command with --help.

codes.title: Internal error
codes.meaning: An unexpected condition inside the engine. This is a bug.
codes.remediation: Please report it at https://github.com/TuanFaied/rtogtor/issues with the command and engine version (no credentials).
